                              Production

                 Abstract                We   propose   HybridSign,    a   hybrid
                                                       autoregressive-diffusion model  that combines
       Earlier Sign Language Production (SLP) mod-                                                      the strengths of both paradigms for low-latency
       els typically relied on autoregressive decoding,                                               SLP. In  this paper, low latency refers to the     which naturally preserves temporal causality

       time. More recent diffusion-based approaches       then continue generation frame by frame, which
      improve generation quality through iterative         is more  informative  for  interactive use than

       dress this trade-off, we propose HybridSign, a                                               frame generation, while the flow-based diffusion
      hybrid autoregressive-diffusion model for low-                                              pathway improves per-frame refinement quality.

  Here, vθ is a neural network trained to match the

clean data. This flow transports samples from the

 A popular training objective is the flow matching
loss:

along straight paths, offering a deterministic alter-

                                           To address the distribution mismatch between
                                                      training and inference commonly observed in au-
                                                      toregressive models, we draw on the training strat-
                                             egy proposed in Self-Forcing (Huang et al., 2025).
                                                    Instead of relying on ground truth during training,
                                                our model always conditions the next step on its
                                       own previously generated articulators. Specifically,
                                                            at each time step t, the model produces

                                                                                ˜At = fAR(˜A<t),
                                                                 ˜A<t = {˜A1, . . . , ˜At−1},        (11)
                                                                                ˜At = {˜Ft, ˜Ht, ˜Bt}.
                                               where ˜Ft, ˜Ht, and ˜Bt denote the generated face,
                                                 hands, and body components at time step t, re-
                                                         spectively. These components are fused into a full-
                                               frame pose and then decomposed again to serve as
                                                    the condition for the next step. Using ˜At for the
                                                           articulator tuple avoids overloading the confidence
                                                     notation Ct introduced in Section 3.3.

D.1  Text-based Metrics
                                                 Figure 5 provides additional qualitative examples
BLEU.  BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002) measures                                            on How2Sign. Compared with Figure 4 in the main
n-gram precision between the back-translated sen-
                                                    paper, these examples cover more diverse motion
tence and the reference sentence. We report BLEU-
                                                        patterns and lexical content, further illustrating that
1 and BLEU-4 to capture unigram and 4-gram over-
                                             HybridSign preserves temporally coherent hand–
lap, respectively. Higher BLEU indicates better
                                           body coordination while staying close to the refer-
semantic agreement with the source sentence.
                                               ence pose sequence.
ROUGE-L. ROUGE (Lin, 2004)  is a recall-
oriented metric. We use ROUGE-L, which is based
on the longest common subsequence between the
back-translated sentence and the reference. Higher
ROUGE-L indicates stronger overlap in sentence
content and ordering.

WER.  Word Error Rate (WER) measures the dis-
crepancy between the back-translated sentence and
the original reference:

                S + D + I

where S, D, and I denote the numbers of sub-
stitutions, deletions, and insertions, and N is the
